answer:
**Exponentials can overflow even when the final normalized answer is ordinary.** For logits (1000,1001), direct exponentiation exceeds ordinary floating-point ranges. Softmax then attempts ratios involving infinities, potentially producing NaNs. Yet only the difference between the logits matters. [1](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/index.html)

Subtract the maximum, giving (-1,0). Their exponentials are about (0.3679,1), so the normalized probabilities are approximately (0.2689,0.7311). Multiplying numerator and denominator by the same factor preserves the result while keeping intermediate values safe.

For log-sum-exp, factor out the maximum explicitly: $\log\sum_i e^{x_i}=m+\log\sum_i e^{x_i-m}$. The shifted exponentials are at most one for finite inputs.

**Stable arithmetic still needs valid inputs.** If every masked logit is negative infinity, subtracting the maximum creates an undefined infinity difference. NaNs in the input also remain a problem. Define a policy for fully masked rows and use stable library log-softmax or cross-entropy implementations. Taking the log of an already underflowed probability cannot recover the lost information.

**Technical details and references.**

Subtracting the maximum keeps exponent arguments nonpositive while preserving the normalized result. [1](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/index.html)

$$\log\sum_i e^{x_i}=m+\log\sum_i e^{x_i-m},\qquad m=\max_i x_i.$$

Without stabilization, large positive logits can overflow and produce infinity divided by infinity in softmax. Subtraction prevents that overflow for finite inputs, but does not repair NaNs or an all-negative-infinity masked row. Such rows need an explicit policy, often zero output with safe normalization. Use library log-sum-exp/log-softmax operations, especially when computing cross-entropy, rather than taking a log of already rounded tiny probabilities.
